description: Regression guard for audit reports: separate the clean route from parent-layout and optional-content findings, group findings by fix, and explain why phase is or is not the cheapest complete tier.

requiredAbsent.reason: the primary route is clean and scanner targets are non-transitive
the parent layout requires its own focused scan

expectedBehavior: Runs the clean primary route scan first, then checks its parent layout and both entries in the article registry without expanding into unrelated code
Starts the report by saying the route file itself is clean while the parent header always runs and the video scrubber appears only for the video article
Groups the header's layout read and window listener into one fix instead of presenting two independent problems

Eliminates the header's per-event layout read and bare listener, preferring CSS scroll-driven behavior when it preserves the design and otherwise using page scroll tracking plus observed header height, such as useScroll with target page and useSize
Keeps the header fix in the shared parent layout and uses the article as a regression case instead of applying a blog-only workaround
Notices that intentPosition is never rendered and removes that hover path instead of replacing dead code with phase
Prefers a native range input for the video scrubber when its design can be preserved; otherwise recommends pointer capture, one cached layout read at drag start, and at most one update per frame
Explains that usePointer fits element-relative hover tracking if that behavior is retained, but does not own drag gestures, and that useScroll is unrelated to pointer movement

Keeps the scanner's severity and noise tiers in technical details while ordering one fix queue by harm, audited-path reach, frequency, affected callers or instances, shared leverage, evidence support, repair cost, and regression risk
Labels finding, actionable-finding, fix, and affected-area counts with their units
Uses direct language, explains required browser terms, and makes no measured runtime claim without a performance trace
Uses the brief report shape for this chat request, omits empty sections, and puts technical details after the fix-order summary
